SOURCE_DATE (2026-08-12): distinct from `checked`. `checked` is when I last LOOKED; `source_date` is when the source was PUBLISHED. The MacBook staleness cost 18pp precisely because those diverged invisibly — checked=1d ago on a source published 114d earlier, in a story that had moved three times since. For live-state sources (a leaderboard, an order book, a market description) the two are equal by construction. ATOMICITY REQUIRED (2026-08-13): one independently checkable assertion per entry, each with its own source and source_date. Bundled entries are how an unchecked fact hides inside a checked one — SpaceX's 'No plausible 2026 rival: OpenAI pushed to 2027, and a >$2.1T close would need an S-1 already public' bundled OpenAI's TIMING (checked twice) with every other rival's SIZE (never checked), and the second cost the project its largest prior correction. If an entry contains ' and ' joining two verifiable claims, split it. SOURCE TAXONOMY (2026-08-13) — 'is it a URL' is the WRONG test and my first sweep miscategorised because of it. Ranked by what may move a number: (1) FIRST-HAND MEASUREMENT — a CLOB book walk, a gamma/API read, an on-chain balance. Reproducible on demand and STRONGER than any article, even though it carries no URL. (2) DATED PRIMARY ARTIFACT — a fetched, dated piece; the standard for a factual claim about the world. (3) NAMED BUT UNLINKED — e.g. 'third-party trackers'; verifiable with effort, acceptable if the claim is checked periodically. (4) AGGREGATED SEARCH SUMMARY — a LEAD ONLY. It must never move a prior: on 2026-08-13 one such summary said the M5 reshuffle was an 'acceleration', moved MacBook 0.62->0.58, and pinning it to dated sources REFUTED it outright. Label the kind when the source is not a URL, so a future sweep does not mistake a measurement for a guess.
